title: Quote Revision Vault
summary: Revise quotes without losing earlier prices, scope, or customer-ready receipts.
user: A solo service provider who needs to revise a quote without losing what was previously offered or accidentally billing against the wrong version.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Invoice Ninja user explicitly asks for a revision on every save after overwriting something by mistake, with rollback depth.
A freelancer says the only desired functions were simple quoting, invoicing, and recurring invoices—evidence that a small, focused workflow is preferable to a suite.

recurrence: Two independent freelancer/invoicing contexts; accidental changes are high-severity because the sent price and scope become difficult to prove.
current_workaround: Duplicate a PDF, rename files with v2/v3, or trust a suite's generic audit log and manually compare PDFs.
incumbents_and_gap: Invoice Ninja, QuickBooks, and Xero create quotes but make a compact before/after scope-and-price comparison and customer-facing version receipt secondary or absent.
smallest_useful_product: Offline-first quote editor that stores immutable revisions, renders a line-item diff, and exports one PDF plus a customer-acknowledgement link. Non-goals: payments, bookkeeping, e-signature legality, or a CRM.
success_measure: In a 30-day pilot, 70% of users who revise a quote send the generated diff, and at least one avoids a scope/price clarification email.
monetization: one-time — quote history is durable local business data and should keep working without a recurring bill.
constraints: Keep quote/customer data local by default; link tokens must be revocable and expiry-controlled; do not represent acknowledgement as a legally binding signature.
why_distinct: The primary artifact is an intelligible revision trail, not a full invoicing product.
